entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Marius P. f. was a Roman senator and ordinary consul in 62 AD with Lucius Afinius Gallus as his colleague. Although Frontinus records that Marius was appointed curator aquarum in 64, we know nothing more about him.


Marius is known for his efforts to improve the water supply system in Rome, which was a major undertaking in the late 1st century AD. His work laid the groundwork for future reforms in urban planning and public works.


As a senator, Marius played a significant role in the governance of Rome, but his legacy has been overshadowed by that of his more famous contemporaries. Despite this, his contributions to the development of Rome's infrastructure and institutions remain an important part of the city's history.


Marius's impact can be seen in the many aqueducts and public fountains that still stand today, a testament to his dedication to improving the lives of Roman citizens.
